REGULATIONS NO 20/R/ICT/RURA/2024 GOVERNING AUTOMATED FARE
COLLECTION SERVICE IN PUBLIC TRANSPORT IN RWANDA
The Regulatory Board;
Pursuant to Law n° 09/2013 of 01/03/2013 establishing Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority
(RURA) and determining its mission, powers, organisation and functioning, especially in
Articles 2, 4, 6 and 20;
Pursuant to Law n°24/2016 of 18/06/2016 governing Information and Communication
Technologies, especially in articles 40;
Based on recommendations made during the consultative meeting held on 06/11//2024 between
the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority and stakeholders in public transport sector and
Automated Fare Collection service providers;
After consideration and deliberation in its session of 11/11/2024;
HEREBY ISSUES THE FOLLOWING REGULATIONS:
CHAPTER ONE: GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article One: Purpose of these Regulations
The purpose of these Regulations is to establish a regulatory framework for Automated Fare
Collection systems in public transport services.
Article 2: Scope of Application
These Regulations applies to all Automated Fare Collection service providers in Rwanda.
Article 3: Interpretation
In these Regulations:
(a) “ABT” means the Account Based Ticketing;
(b) “ABT data structure” means an Automated Fare Collection data structure, which utilises
a specified fare structure on an ABT compliant issued fare media, for electronically
recording and retrieving transit products and public transport trip related data;
2

(c) “ABT issued fare media” means a fare media issued by a participating fare media issuer
that is compliant with the technical specifications and provisions as specified in the AFC
Guidelines or included in a directive issued or amended by RURA from time to time;
(d) “AFC” means Automated Fare Collection;
(e) “AFC Guideline” means the Automated Fare Collection Guidelines document issued or
amended by RURA, which includes:
i. relevant technical specifications for fare media issuance and acceptance;
ii. additional technical specifications, rules and standards relevant to AFC; and
iii. a guideline for interpreting the AFC Regulations for the implementation of AFC
Systems.
(f) “AFC Operator” means the AFC System vendor and operator licensed by RURA;
(g) “AFC system” means An Automated Fare Collection (AFC) System, as a collection
technology-driven solution component used in public transportation to streamline and
manage fare collection;
(h) “Legacy AFC system” means any existing AFC system prior to the issuance of these
regulations, whether fully operational or not;
(i) ‘’Licensee’’ means an entity issued with an application license for the provision of
Automated Fare Collection services;
(j) “RURA” means the “Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority.
CHAPTER II: LICENSING REGIME
Article 4: License application
(1) Any legal entity wishing to provide Automated Fare Collection services must apply for
an Application Service Provision License from the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory
Authority (RURA), in accordance with the Regulations Governing Licensing in
Electronic Communications.
(2) An applicant for an AFC license must not be an Account-Based Ticketing (ABT)
service provider, nor any entity operating an ABT system, in order to avoid conflicts of
interest and ensure a fair and competitive market.
(3) RURA will set and publish operational, technical, financial, and compliance standards,
which form an integral part of the license obligations.
3

Article 5: Validity of the license
The validity of the Automated Fare Collection license is five (5) years.
Article 6: License renewal
The Licensee must apply for license renewal at least six (6) months prior to the expiration of
the current license. The requirements and procedure for renewal shall be the same as those
applicable to the issuance of the original license.
Article 7: License fees and financial obligations
(1) Application and license fees: The Licensee must pay the application and license fees
as specified in the Regulations Governing Licensing in Electronic Communications.
(2) Regulatory fee: The Licensee must pay one percent (1%) of its annual turnover.
Modalities and timeframe are provided for under the RURA Board Decision that
determines the contribution levied on the annual turnover of regulated services.
(3) Universal Access fee: The Licensee must contribute to the Universal Access Fund in
accordance with the Presidential Order. The contribution rate and payment modalities
are determined by a Regulatory Board Decision.
Article 8: License modification
(1) A license modification proceeding may be initiated by RURA or upon the request of the
license holder. Such request shall provide reasonable grounds of such modification.
(2) The Regulatory Authority may modify a license before the expiration of the license term
when it determines that an amendment of the license is needed in order to respond to:
(a) Significant changes in the relevant laws, regulations, policies or a court decision
that directly affect the license provision;
(b) The inability of the license holder to comply with controlling license provisions due
to events beyond the licensee’s control;
Article 9: Transfer of license
(1) The transfer of a license may be permitted in the event of any of the following:
(a) Temporary substitution, lease or transfer of assets or activities to a different person or
corporation must be approved by the RURA;
4

(b) The request of a transfer must state the reason of such transfer and the approval is
subject to the clearance of all required fees provided for under applicable laws and
regulations.
(c) The transferee is considered as the applicant of the license and thus must comply with
the requirements on such category of license.
(d) The transferee must comply with the obligations of the transferred license.
(2) Transfer of license, including the direct or indirect sale, assignment, conveyance, lease or
other transfer of assets or activities subject to a license to a different person shall be subject
to a prior written approval of the Regulatory Authority.
(3) Such approval shall be granted after consideration of the matter and if the proposed transfer
meets all the conditions for granting the relevant license;
(4) Failure to comply with these requirements may result in the suspension or revocation of the
license.
CHAPTER III: SUSPENSION AND REVOCATION OF THE LICENSE
Article 10: License suspension
The Regulatory Authority suspends a license for a determined period if:
(a) the licensee fails to comply with the laws, regulations and relevant decisions or
directives of the Regulatory Authority;
(b) the licensee fails to comply with license obligations;
(c) the licensee fails to pay regulatory fees or any other required fee;
(d) the licensee fails to address poor service delivery issues;
(e) there are disputes within the licensed company that negatively impact service delivery.
(f) there is a failure to comply with an enforcement notice;
(g) there is a serious misconduct that may distort fair competition or affects consumer
interests;
(h) there is a serious misconduct that puts into jeopardy the public interest;
(i) there is a repeated failure to provide the Regulatory Authority with monitoring and
reporting data required;
(j) there is a repeated failure to cooperate with the Regulatory Authority inspection and
audits;
(k) there is a misconduct that threatens the national values and culture.
5

Article 11: License revocation
The Regulatory Authority revokes the license if:
(a) The licensee has provided false or inaccurate information that has impacted in the
decision of granting the license;
(b) The licensee is involved in fraudulent transactions and fare evasion;
(c) The licensee abandons activities without notifying the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory
Authority;
(d) The licensee is liquidated or declared bankrupt by a competent Court;
(e) The licensee ceases to operate the activities for which it was licensed;
(f) The licensee consistently fails to comply with license obligations;
(g) The licensee fails to comply with a suspension decision and/or orders issued by the
Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority;
(h) The licensee engages in activities that compromise national security or public
interest.
CHAPTER IV: ACCOUNT BASED TICKETING AND AUTOMATED FARE
COLLECTION SYSTEMS
Article 12: Description of the ABT system
The ABT system is a fare collection technology that includes the following components:
(a) An ABT compatible fare media;
(b) an ABT compatible fare media distribution network and value loading
infrastructure;
(c) Infrastructure for fare transaction acceptance, initiation, and processing;
(d) an account hosting function;
(e) an electronic fare transaction processing and settlement function;
(f) associated information systems utilised for the management and analysis of fare
schedules and data, and converting this data into actionable information.
6

Article 13: Automated Fare Collection system requirements
The AFC system must meet the following requirements:
(a) The AFC must use an ABT compatible fare media;
(b) The ABT compatible fare media and the associated ABT prepaid account balance
must be seamlessly topped-up;
(c) The AFC system must be interoperable across all public transport services;
(d) Fare transaction processing for settlement must occur through a Transaction Clearing
House technology and infrastructure that provides account hosting and transaction
processing services to AFC operators;
(e) passengers must be able to obtain ABT fare media from either an AFC operator or a
third-party issuer;
(f) the ABT fare media system must adhere to the standards and specifications issued by
RURA;
(g) The ABT data structure must be encoded in all issued ABT fare media;
(h) The AFC system must support fare structures that align with any national fare
policies, as issued and updated periodically;
(i) the AFC system must comply with the relevant standards issue by RURA to ensure
compatibility and interoperability.
Article 14: Operator issued fare media
Occasional or infrequent passengers of public transport services must be able to obtain a
prepaid single trip ticket, provided that:
(a) the prepaid single trip ticket is issued exclusively for the redemption of the single
trip public transport service;
(b) the prepaid single trip ticket consists of any appropriate fare media; and
(c) the prepaid single trip ticket is non-reloadable.
7

Article 15: Data Management
(1) Public transport data must be collected electronically through the AFC system
concurrently with the payment or redemption transaction;
(2) RURA is the data controller of the data collected through the ABT and AFC system
and shall have full real time access and acquisition;
(3) Data are collected for planning and operational purposes, and must include data per
transaction on location, route, fare and passenger, as well as any additional data
prescribed by the Regulatory Authority from time to time;
(4) Public Transport Operators shall have access to data related to their own operations.
Article 16: Compliance with fare structure policy
The AFC system must support fare structures that align with national fare policies, as approved
by the Regulatory Authority. These may include, but are not limited to, the following types:
(a) Flat fare: A fixed fare amount for a single trip, regardless of the time, zones or
distance traveled;
(b) Distance-based fare: A fare calculated based on the distance traveled by the passenger;
(c) Graduated distance-based fare: is a fare system where the fare for a trip increases or
decreases progressively based on the distance traveled.
(d) Zone-based fare: A fare structure where the fare is determined by the number of
geographical zones a passenger travel through;
(e) Time-based fare: A fare that is calculated based on the hours of the day;
(f) Combined fare: A fare structure that integrates two or more fare components into a
single fare calculation;
(g) Any other fare structure: A fare structure that may be published by the Regulatory
Authority from time to time, which can include variations or new models that reflect
changes in transportation needs or policy.
8

CHAPTER V: FAULTS AND ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS
Article 17: System downtime
Any Licensee whose service performance fails to meet the minimum system uptime standards
established in the AFC Guidelines shall be subject to an administrative fine ranging from five
hundred thousand (FRW 500,000) to fifteen million (FRW 15,000,000) Rwandan Francs for
each day of non-compliance.
Article 18: Non-Compliance with Fare Structure
Any Licensee whose system calculation deviates from the established fare structure or fails to
comply with fare calculation rules shall be liable to a penalty equal to twice the amount of any
additional fare incorrectly charged to passengers.
Article 19: Failure to Meet Accessibility Standards
Any Licensee who fails to provide the necessary infrastructure and technology to ensure
accessible fare media services at designated premises, or to allow passengers to top up their
accounts and check fare balances, shall be liable to an administrative fine ranging from five
hundred thousand (FRW 500,000) to five million (FRW 5,000,000) Rwandan Francs.
Article 20: Maintain Data Accuracy and Integrity
The AFC provider must uphold high standards of data accuracy, completeness, and reliability,
ensuring passengers and transaction data are correctly recorded and securely stored. Failure to
Maintain Data Accuracy and Integrity will result in an administrative fine of five million (FRW
5,000,000) Rwandan Francs.
Article 21: Fraudulent Activity or System Manipulation
Without prejudice to any criminal prosecution, any Licensee involved in fraudulent activities,
including but not limited to tampering with the AFC system, fare evasion, or ticket
manipulation, shall be subject to an administrative fine of ten million (FRW 10,000,000)
Rwandan Francs, revocation of their license, and shall be required to compensate the affected
party.
Article 22: General Breach of Regulations
Notwithstanding the sanctions specified in these Regulations, any violation of other provisions,
including failure to comply with technical standards, shall be subject to penalties as prescribed
under the Law governing Information and Communication Technologies and/or the Law
establishing the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority, where applicable.
9

CHAPTER VI: FINAL PROVISIONS
Article 23: Transitional period
(1) Any legacy Automatic Fare Collection system must be capable of accepting Account-
Based Ticketing issued Fare Media by 30 June 2025, ensuring full compliance with
both technical and operational requirements.
(2) During the transitional period, the licensed operators must ensure full and seamless
interoperability as per the technical specifications found in Annex of these Regulations.
(3) Notwithstanding this transitional period, all existing licensees must comply with:
i. any fare structure policy issued by the Regulatory Authority; and
ii. Automated fare collection system transitional performance requirements found
in Annex, upon the approval of these Regulations.
Article 24: Entry into force
These Regulations come into effect on the date of its signature by the Chairperson of the
Regulatory Board.
Kigali, 13th November 2024
(sé)
Dr. NTAGUNGIRA Carpophore
Chairperson of the Regulatory Board
10

ANNEX: AUTOMATED FARE COLLECTION SYSTEM TRANSITIONAL
PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS
These requirements ensure that Automated Fare Collection (AFC) systems operate seamlessly
and efficiently, upholding users' rights and maintaining uninterrupted service throughout the
transition to an Account-Based Ticketing (ABT) system. Compliance with these requirements
is mandatory during the transitional phase, as stipulated in the Automated Fare Collection
System Regulations.
I. System Compatibility and Interoperability Standards
I.1 Interoperability Standards
• Seamless Fare Media Recognition: AFC systems, including fare validators, POS
terminals, and other devices, must recognize, process, and authorize fare media across
interconnected systems.
• Card Compatibility: Enable existing transport cards to function seamlessly across
both legacy and new systems, allowing passengers to use the same card across all AFC
systems encountered on their journey.
• Unified Fare Policy: Ensure all systems adhere to a unified fare policy to provide a
consistent user experience.
I.2 Transaction Speed and Processing Standards for an AFC
• Minimal Transaction Latency: Ensure transaction latency remains under 300
milliseconds, with a maximum of three (3) second, to avoid delays, especially during
peak hours and high-traffic areas.
• Real-Time Fare Calculation and Synchronization: Implement real-time fare
calculation based on distance travelled, with fare validators displaying fare deductions,
remaining balances, and other relevant information across both systems to prevent
passenger confusion.
• Offline Functionality: Equip validators with offline capabilities to store transaction
data until reconnected. Stored data must synchronize reliably with a central database to
prevent data loss.
• Peak Load Capacity: Ensure validators and back-office systems handle peak
transaction loads effectively.
• Consistent Boarding Times: Maintain minimal boarding times during peak hours by
ensuring consistent transaction speeds across both systems.
11

II. Data Security and Reliability
• Data Encryption: Protect data during storage and transmission in adherence to the
Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS).
• Two-Factor Authentication: Implement two-layer authentication for administrators
and operators accessing fare processing data across systems.
• High Uptime Requirement: Maintain a minimum uptime of 99.9% to ensure reliable
AFC services.
• Performance Reporting: Record real-time system usage data and generate daily,
weekly, and monthly reports with metrics on transaction success rate, validation times,
and system downtime for regulatory review.
• Secure Key Sharing Mechanism: Establish a secure key-sharing protocol to
authenticate fare media and validate transactions, potentially using symmetric or
asymmetric encryption keys for data exchange.
• Key Management Compliance: Enforce key rotation, secure storage, and destruction
policies aligned with industry standards.
III. User Interface and Communication Standards
• Clear Usage Instructions: Display clear, concise instructions on fare validators and
mobile applications, guiding passengers on using card-based and distance-based fare
models, including prompts for tapping in and out, selecting payment methods, and
verifying fare calculations.
• Multi-Language Support: Ensure multi-language support on validators and mobile
apps to accommodate diverse user groups.
• Feedback Mechanism: Implement a feedback system allowing passengers to report
issues related to system interoperability and suggest areas for improvement.
• 24/7 Real-Time User Support: Provide round-the-clock real-time user support for
inquiries or issues.
• Dispute Resolution: Establish a swift, transparent resolution process for fare disputes,
including double charges, incorrect fare deductions, and fare capping errors.
IV. Anti-Fraud and Security Standards
• Fraud Detection Algorithms: Deploy fraud detection algorithms to identify and flag
unusual activity, such as cloned cards or duplicate account activity across AFC systems.
• Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Enforce strict role-based access controls to limit
personnel access to transaction data, account management, and back-office settings.
12

• Device Authentication: Authenticate each validator and fare media device within both
AFC systems to prevent unauthorized devices from accessing the network or fare data.
V. Compliance and Regulatory Standards
• Data Privacy Compliance: Ensure all AFC systems comply with national data privacy
regulations.
• Regulatory Compliance: AFC systems must adhere to regulatory requirements as
periodically approved by RURA.
• Audit Trail and Transparency: Maintain clear audit trails and transaction logs across
both systems to ensure transparency and accountability throughout the transition
period.
These performance requirements establish a solid foundation for a smooth and secure transition
to an Account-Based Ticketing system, prioritizing user experience, data security, and
regulatory compliance.
13
